title: One feature panel everywhere in Simple: read and edit any feature from any page
subtitle: Every page that shows a feature (Roadmap's views, Priorities and its Goal buckets, Home, a PRD's one-pager, Meetings, Decisions) opens the same panel to read and change it. Invented company, features and people.

decisions.name: The panel's form and layout
decisions.question: What shape does the one feature panel take, what does it show first, and how does it fit a phone?
decisions.common: The same panel from every page; a click on a feature's name opens it. Its head shows title, status, owner, confidence and a flag when the dates clash; then Dates (start and delivery, each with where it comes from), Goal (the goal, its measure, today's reading and the target), Links (depends on and needed by), Milestone and Details (outcome, status, owner, confidence, notes). Simple's colours, type and buttons as built. Edits and links shown as in FP2 A and FP3 A.

proposals.name: Side panel on the right
proposals.what: The panel slides in over the right of any page, 460 px wide and full height; the page stays lit and can still be scrolled and clicked beside it. Its head shows the title, status, owner, confidence and a clash flag; two tabs switch between Details and Talk to Oracle. Details reads top down: Dates, Goal, Links, Milestone, Details. On a phone it is a sheet from the bottom.
proposals.why: One shape on every page, narrow enough that the Timeline, a goal bucket or Home's card stays in view while you read and change the feature, and the chart stays reachable for picking items. Today's roadmap card and its talk already use the same parts.
proposals.plus: Same place and width everywhere; the page is never hidden; the talk is one tab away; the phone sheet is the same panel.
proposals.cost: The talk and the details never show side by side; on a phone the sheet leaves only the top quarter of the page showing.

proposals.name: Panel with talk beside
proposals.what: A wide panel (880 px) on the right with two columns: the details at left and the feature's talk with Oracle at right, both always open. The page behind is dimmed. On a phone it fills the screen with Details and Talk tabs.
proposals.plus: The talk is always beside the details, so asking Oracle about a date and changing it happen in one view; it extends today's roadmap card with its talk open.
proposals.cost: Covers about two thirds of the page and dims the rest, so the item it was opened from is mostly hidden; the talk takes room even when nobody uses it.

Opened from Goal buckets: the buckets are hidden behind the panel.
Opened from Home: only a strip of Home shows at left.
Changing the delivery date with the talk open beside it.
The hard case at 1512 for a reader: the title wraps; links scroll in the left column; the talk keeps its full column.

Dark theme, over Goal buckets.

proposals.name: Full-height sheet
proposals.what: A large sheet (1040 px) rises from the bottom over a dimmed page, with every part in two columns at once: Dates and Links at left, Goal, Milestone and Details at right. The talk is reached from the feature's own page. On a phone it fills the screen, with chips to jump between parts.
proposals.plus: Everything about the feature in one look, with little scrolling.
proposals.cost: Hides the page it was opened from; with many links the left column runs long and leaves the right one short; no talk in the sheet.

frames.caption: Opened from Roadmap's Timeline: all parts in two columns; the Timeline is dimmed behind.
Opened from Goal buckets: the same sheet hides the buckets.
Opened from Home.

The hard case at 1512 for a reader: 8 links make the left column run past the fold while the right one ends early.

proposals.name: Card beside the item
proposals.what: A small card (380 px) opens next to the feature that was clicked, as today's roadmap card does: right of it when there is room, left of it when not. Every part is in the card and it scrolls. On a phone it is a short sheet that pulls up for the rest.
proposals.plus: Stays closest to where you clicked and to today's roadmap card; covers the least of the page.
proposals.cost: The card moves with each page and item, so it is never in the same place; everything must scroll in a small box; with a long title and 8 links most of it is below the fold.

decisions.name: How editing works
decisions.question: How does a person change a feature in the panel, and how is an override of Oracle's suggestion made, shown and undone?
decisions.common: Every value can be changed in the panel, including Oracle's suggested date, goal and links. An override always names Oracle's value and who set the new one, and can be undone. Owners and approvers change; anyone else reads the same panel (checked through can() or the feature's own can-change field, never by role name). Shown in the side panel (FP1 A).

proposals.name: Each field in place
proposals.what: Every value in the panel is a field: click a date, the goal, an owner or a note, change it there, and Save or Cancel just under it. When the new value replaces Oracle's suggestion the panel says so before saving, and after it the field keeps one line: "Oracle suggested Dec 10; set to Nov 27 by Leo Brandt · Restore". Restore puts Oracle's value back. People who can't change the feature (checked through can(), not by role name) see the same panel with no fields and a note with Suggest a change.
proposals.why: The fastest edit (one click, one field), and the override sits on the value it changes, worded as the owner asked, with Restore one click away.
proposals.plus: One click to change one thing; each override is shown where it applies; nothing else on the panel changes while you edit.
proposals.cost: Each field needs its own hover and focus look; changing several things at once is several saves.

frames.caption: At rest for an owner: values look plain; a click on one turns it into a field.

Saved: the delivery reads Nov 27 with "Oracle suggested Dec 10; set to Nov 27 by Leo Brandt · Restore"; the clash with the Beta milestone is gone, the one with Alert rules engine stays.
Back on the Timeline: the bar now ends Nov 27, the row is marked and a note offers Undo.
A reader at 1512: no fields, a note says who can change it, and Suggest a change.
Phone 390, the same edit in the sheet.
Dark theme, the saved override over Goal buckets.

proposals.name: One Edit mode
proposals.what: The panel reads plainly until Edit at its top is pressed; then every value becomes a field at once and a bar at the foot counts the changes, with Save changes and Cancel. Oracle's value shows beside a changed field. After saving, a box at the top lists every change from Oracle's plan with Restore, and each changed value carries a Set by hand mark.
proposals.plus: Several changes go in one save; every override of the feature is listed in one box.
proposals.cost: Two clicks before any change; the whole panel turns into a form for a one-date change; the list of overrides sits away from the values it changes.

frames.caption: At rest: Edit sits by the title.
Edit mode: every value is a field; the foot says 1 change: delivery, with Save changes.
Saved: a box at the top says 1 change from Oracle's plan with Restore; the date carries Set by hand.
Back on the Timeline: the bar ends Nov 27 and a note offers Undo.
A reader at 1512: no Edit button, the reader's note instead.
Phone 390: the form with its Save bar at the foot of the sheet.
Dark theme, the change box over Goal buckets.

proposals.name: A section at a time
proposals.what: Each part of the panel (Dates, Goal, Links, Milestone, Details) has its own Change link; pressing it turns only that part into a form, which asks why when it overrides Oracle. After saving, the part is marked Changed by hand and says who changed what and why, with Restore Oracle's dates.
proposals.plus: Related values change together (start and delivery), and the reason is kept for everyone.
proposals.cost: Asking why on every override slows small fixes; Restore undoes the whole part, not one value; more Change links on screen.

A reader at 1512: no Change links.

decisions.name: Reading and changing links
decisions.question: How are a feature's links read and changed both ways, and how is a date clash they bring shown and fixed?
decisions.common: Both directions show: what it depends on and what needs it, each with its dates and where the link came from. Links can be added or removed both ways; an Oracle link a person removes stays visible with Restore; a clash is said in words with fixes to pick (start after it, keep the dates and mark it at risk, remove the link). Shown in the side panel (FP1 A) with edits in place (FP2 A).

proposals.name: Two lists with search
proposals.what: Links has two lists, Depends on and Needed by, each with a count. Each row shows the other item's dates and where the link came from (Found by Oracle, or Added by a person) and an × to remove it; an Oracle link that was removed stays, struck through, with Restore. + Add opens a search across roadmaps that shows items already linked and items that would make a loop. When a new link breaks the dates, a box under the lists says how and offers fixes: start after it, keep the dates and mark it at risk, or remove the link.
proposals.why: Works the same on every page, chart or not, and at any size; the overridden Oracle link and the clash read as words with one-click fixes.
proposals.plus: Same on every page and phone; 8 links are just a longer list; loops are stopped in the search.
proposals.cost: You can't see the links on the chart while you pick; you must know the item's name.

Adding a link from Goal buckets: the same search.
Phone 390, from Home: the search in the sheet.

proposals.name: Pick on the chart
proposals.what: + Add puts the page in picking mode: every item on the roadmap is outlined and a click links it; a typed name works too. The new link is drawn on the chart, red while the dates clash. Pages without a chart (Home, Goal buckets) fall back to typing the name.
proposals.plus: You see where the other item sits in time while you pick, and the link stays visible on the chart.
proposals.cost: Each page needs its own picking mode and line drawing; on pages with no chart and on phones it is only the search; the side panel covers part of the chart you pick from.

proposals.name: Link map in the panel
proposals.what: Links is a small map: what the feature depends on at left, the feature in the middle with its dates, what needs it at right, with lines between. A red line marks a clash and a dashed one an Oracle link a person removed; + boxes in each column add an item by search.
proposals.plus: Both directions read at a glance, with the clash drawn where it is.
proposals.cost: Crowded past a few links (8 means scrolling inside the map); long titles are cut short; harder to read on a phone.
